classification_basis: Classes describe the PRE-LAG construction semantics (what each column reads relative to the label base mid(t) BEFORE the universal shift(1) at phase7_l2_sim.py line 276). This matches the pre-fix condition that produced results/phase7/l2_predictions (ZC 5s AUC 0.9662 per results/phase7/l2_model_meta.csv). The archived script itself is the POST-fix variant: line 275 'feature_cols = [c for c in snap.columns if c not in exempt]' and line 276 'snap[feature_cols] = snap[feature_cols].shift(1)' lag every feature (including bid_size_1/ask_size_1, which are NOT in the raw_book_cols exemption at lines 268-272). Labels are exempt: line 267 label_cols = fwd_move_ticks_*.  ||  OPERATIVE RULE, RESTATED (R102/§179): the rule actually separating the three classes is INDEPENDENCE OF PATH, not raw-vs-derived inputs. A column is LEAK-SOURCE if it reaches t-state by at least one route that does NOT pass through another classified LEAK-SOURCE; DESCENDANT if EVERY such route does; CLEAN if it has no t-state route at all. NO CLASSIFICATION CHANGES under the restatement - it was verified to reproduce all 35 exactly (0 disagreements). BOTH RULES ARE RECORDED because they are not equivalent: raw-vs-derived agrees today ONLY because bid_size_2..5 / ask_size_5 are unclassified raw columns outside the 35, so a route through them counts as 'raw'. It would MISCLASSIFY a derived-but-unclassified input, which independence-of-path handles correctly by asking whether the route passes through a CLASSIFIED leak source rather than whether the input looks raw. Worked example: total_bid_depth sums bid_size_1..5 - bid_size_1 is LEAK-SOURCE but bid_size_2..5 are unclassified, so an independent route to t-state exists and the class is LEAK-SOURCE; book_imbalance_ratio reads total_bid_depth / total_ask_depth, both classified LEAK-SOURCE, every route passes through one, so it is DESCENDANT.
